Subject: Pilot economics check: burn velocity, budget range & credit bridge for FintechX

Hi Liam / Procurement team —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — appreciate you walking us through the main flows. Per our conversation I wanted to capture the cost/volume pieces we need to lock down to size the pilot and propose a short credit bridge to avoid early stop/start while you finish procurement. Quick recap and asks below: 

1) Ask: monthly usage profile
   - Expected MAU for the feature: ? (you mentioned mid-50ks range verbally)
   - Estimated weekly active users and % who will hit the NLU flow
   - Typical prompt + completion token lengths (avg prompt, expected generated tokens)

2) Economic targets
   - Target $/1M tokens you have budgeted (you mentioned 'around $1k' — want to confirm a range)
   - Any internal unit economics or ROI thresholds we should know (e.g., $/converted-user)

3) Pilot mechanics
   - Length: 30–60 days preferred
   - Success signals: latency < 300ms p50, < $X/1M tokens, conversion lift on NLU route

If you can reply with the three quick numbers above (MAU, avg tokens per session, target $/1M), I will:
- Send a short cost note with 2 conservative consumption scenarios + recommended quantum of trial credits to keep you running during procurement.
- Draft a 30-day mutual action plan (milestones + weekly check-ins).

We can also do a quick 20m follow-up if that’s easier.

Thanks —
Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Nikhil —

Great recap, thanks. Quick answers below based on the teams' estimates this morning: 

- MAU for the feature: ~52,000 (we expect this to ramp to ~80k over 3 months if the initial cohort looks good)
- Active users hitting the flow: ~9% of MAU initially (so ~4.7k). Expect ~15% adoption after month 2.
- Calls: estimating ~4–6 calls per active user per month (depends on campaign).
- Tokens per call: average prompt 350 tokens, generation ~900 tokens => ~1,250 tokens per call on average.

Rough math: 5k active * 5 calls/mo * 1,250 tokens = ~31.25M tokens/mo initially. That could double if adoption and call frequency increase.

Budget: We have a soft target of $900–1,100 per 1M tokens for this pilot (upper bound if we can get consistent latency and decent QoE). Procurement will likely need a PO for any invoice after credits — they're moving, but it will take ~3–6 weeks.

Regarding credits: an initial bridge would be helpful so we don’t throttle testing while procurement moves. Can you propose an amount and conditions?

Happy to hop on a quick sync if it helps.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor | Head of Product, FintechX

Thanks Liam — that profile is super helpful and lines up with what we discussed. I ran two conservative scenarios and included the math below so procurement has a clear reference. I’ve attached a one-sheet (fintechx_pilot_mop.xlsx) and a draft credit note for review.

Scenario A (conservative adoption)
- 31.25M tokens/mo (baseline)
- Using our quantized serving tier (Q8-like), estimated unit = $1,050 / 1M tokens
- Monthly cost = ~ $32.8k

Scenario B (ramp/adoption)
- 60M tokens/mo
- With batching and prefix/KV cache, effective unit can drop to ~$820 / 1M tokens
- Monthly cost = ~ $49.2k

Proposal (what we can do now)
- Provide a $15,000 trial credit ("credit bridge") applied to your first month of usage to allow a smooth test while procurement finalizes a PO.
- Conditional approval: 30-day credit, weekly burn check-ins, and a mutual action plan with the key milestones (I attached the MOP).
- If we see sustained ramp > 50M tokens/mo and you commit to a 3-month reserved cadence, we can discuss step-down unit pricing to your $900/1M target or better.

Next steps I suggest:
- Procurement: confirm the internal PO timeline + billing contact (copying Procurement here).
- Liam: confirm you’re OK with the $15k credit and the burn-check cadence.
- I’ll request finance sign-off and share a short credit agreement (attached: credit_bridge_agreement_draft.pdf).

If you prefer a short 20m call to walk through the numbers and the MOP, I’m available Thursday afternoon.

Thanks —
Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
